So he called upon his Lord in a secret call, saying: ﴿My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened within me﴾, that is, became frail and feeble; ﴿and my head has blazed with grey hair﴾, that is, the hair of my head turned grey because of my old age; ﴿and I have never been unblessed in my supplication to You, my Lord﴾, that is, at any time in the past; meaning that You have accustomed me to answering what I call upon You for, and You have not deprived me of the answer to my supplication, so that I would be left wretched without obtaining my desire. ﴿And indeed I fear my relatives﴾, O my Lord, lest they neglect this call, the call to the truth, which is worshipping You alone according to what You have legislated, with no partner, after my death. ﴿So grant me from Yourself﴾, that is, from Your presence, as a favour bestowed upon me, since the means for a child are not available: my wife is barren and I am an old, decrepit man; ﴿an heir﴾, that is, a son who will take charge of this call after my death, so that he inherits it from me; ﴿who will inherit from the family of Ya'qub﴾, my grandfather, what they left behind after them of their father's call, which is the upright religion of worshipping God alone without partner; ﴿and make him, my Lord, pleasing﴾, that is, make the son You grant me, O my Lord, ﴿pleasing﴾, that is, a righteous servant whom You approve of to bear the message of the call to You. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 19, verse 8–15:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Anna yakunu li ghulam?﴾ (How can I have a boy?): i.e., in what manner or by what way will I have a son?

ʿItiyyan (stiffness with age): i.e., my joints and bones have become dry and stiff.

Ayah (a sign): i.e., a sign that informs me of my wife's pregnancy.

Sawiyyan (sound in body): i.e., while you are of sound form, with no impediment of speech upon you.

Min al-mihrab (from the prayer niche): the place of prayer in which he prays, which is the mosque.

Fa-awha ilayhim (so he signaled to them): he gestured to them and indicated to them.

Wa-atayнāhu al-hukma sabiyyan (And We gave him judgment while a boy): al-hukm (judgment) and al-hikmah (wisdom) have one meaning, and they are understanding of the religion and knowledge of the secrets of the Sharia.

Wa-hanānan min ladunnā (and tenderness from Us): i.e., compassion toward people, bestowed upon him from Our presence.

Wa-zakāh (and purity): i.e., purity from sins and transgressions.

Jabbaran ʿasiyyan (a tyrant, disobedient): i.e., one who is haughty and does not accept the truth, disobedient, who does not obey the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nor the command of his parents.

Wa-salāmun ʿalayhi (and peace be upon him): i.e., security for him from Satan, that he would touch him with harm on the day he is born; security for him from the trials of the grave on the day he dies; and security for him from the greatest terror on the day he is raised alive.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues with the mention of Allah's mercy toward His servant Zakariyya. When his Lord, exalted is He, gave him the good news of Yahya, he said what Allah related about him in His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, how can I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age, in stiffness?"﴾ That is, in what manner or by what way will a child come to me: from a woman other than my wife, or from her, but You grant me strength to approach her and make her womb capable of conception? For, as You know, my Lord, I have reached an age in which my bones and joints have dried up, which is the stiffness (ʿitiyy), just as my wife is barren and cannot bear children. Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, answered him with what is in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿He said, "Thus it is."﴾ That is, the matter is as you said, O Zakariyya, but ﴿your Lord says: It is easy for Me﴾ That is, giving you a child despite your weakness and old age and your wife's barrenness is easy and effortless, with no difficulty in it. What points you to this is that ﴿I created you before, when you were nothing.﴾ Just as your Lord was able to create you when you were nothing, He is able to grant you a child despite your weakness and your wife's barrenness. Here Zakariyya asked his Lord to make for him a sign that would show him the time of his wife's conception of the child. He said what Allah, exalted, related in His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, appoint for me a sign." He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, while sound."﴾ So Allah, exalted, gave him a sign of the time of his wife's conception of the child: that he would wake on the day the conception began unable to speak, while his body was sound, with no muteness or illness preventing him from speaking. ﴿So he came out to his people from the prayer niche﴾ That is, the place of prayer in which he prayed. ﴿And he signaled to them﴾ That is, he gestured and indicated to them ﴿to glorify [Allah] morning and evening﴾ That is, remember Allah at these two times with prayer and glorification. Here he knew of his wife's pregnancy, since his refraining from speech while his body and senses were sound was a sign of the beginning of the pregnancy. And His saying, exalted: ﴿O Yahya, take the Scripture with determination﴾ This is the word of Allah, exalted, to the boy after he reached three years of age; Allah commanded him to learn the Torah and act upon it with firm resolve and determination. And His saying ﴿And We gave him judgment while still a child﴾ That is, We bestowed upon him understanding of the Book and knowledge of the secrets of the Sharia, while he was a child who had not reached the age of puberty.

And His saying, exalted: ﴿And tenderness from Us and purity, and he was fearing [Allah]﴾ That is, mercy from Us toward him and love for him. We gave him judgment while a child, just as he, peace be upon him, was tender toward his parents and others among the Muslims. And His saying ﴿and purity﴾ That is, purity from sins through employing his body in obedience to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And he was fearing [Allah]﴾ That is, fearing his Lord, so he would not disobey Him by abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibited act.

And His saying, exalted: ﴿And dutiful to his parents﴾ That is, doing good to them, obeying them, and not harming them in the least. And His saying ﴿and he was not a tyrant or disobedient﴾ That is, he, peace be upon him, was not arrogant or oppressive, nor rebellious against his Lord or his parents. And His saying: ﴿And peace is upon him the day he was born﴾ That is, security for him from Satan on the day he was born, security for him from the trials of the grave on the day he dies, and security for him from the greatest terror on the day he is raised alive. So glory be to Allah, how great is His grace and how abundant His gift to His friends. O Allah, grant us security as You granted him security, for You are the Possessor of great grace.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Seeking to know the means by which an action comes about does not harm the one who asks; Zakariyya's question about the manner in which a child would come is like Ibrahim's question about how the dead are brought to life.

2- It is permissible to seek signs that indicate a matter, for the sake of knowledge.

3- The wondrous sign that Zakariyya would wake unable to speak, so that others understood him by gesture alone.

4- The virtue of glorifying Allah in the morning and evening.

5- The obligation to take the Qur'an with earnestness and determination, by memorizing it and acting upon what it contains.

6- The truth of the words of the scholars that one who memorizes the Qur'an before the age of puberty has been given judgment while a child.

7- The obligation of kindness to parents, mercy toward them, tenderness toward them, and humility before them.

And His saying ﴿and he was not a tyrant or disobedient﴾ That is, he, peace be upon him, was not arrogant or oppressive, nor rebellious against his Lord or his parents. From the guidance of the verses:

1- Seeking to know the means by which an action comes about does not harm the one who asks; Zakariyya's question about the manner in which a child would come is like Ibrahim's question about how the dead are brought to life.

2- It is permissible to seek signs that indicate a matter, for the sake of knowledge.

3- The wondrous sign that Zakariyya would wake unable to speak, so that others understood him by gesture alone.

4- The virtue of glorifying Allah in the morning and evening.

5- The obligation to take the Qur'an with earnestness and determination, by memorizing it and acting upon what it contains.

6- The truth of the words of the scholars that one who memorizes the Qur'an before the age of puberty has been given judgment while a child.

7- The obligation of kindness to parents, mercy toward them, tenderness toward them, and humility before them.

"He said: Thus it is": i.e., the matter is so, and it is the creation of a boy from you without a father.

"It is easy for Me": it is nothing more than that Our messenger blows into the opening of your garment, and the child comes to be.

"And that We may make him a sign for mankind": i.e., a sign of the greatness of Our power.

"And a mercy from Us": i.e., so that the child would be a mercy to whoever believes in him and follows what he brought.

"A matter decreed": i.e., Allah has judged it and completed it, so it will certainly come to be without doubt.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the beginning of the story of Maryam, peace be upon her, when Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿And mention in the Book﴾, i.e., the Noble Qur'an, ﴿Maryam﴾, i.e., her report and her account, so that this would be evidence of your prophethood and of the truth of your message. His words ﴿when she withdrew from her family﴾, i.e., she isolated herself, ﴿to an eastern place﴾ — this is the beginning of the story — and His words ﴿to a place facing east﴾, i.e., a place to the east of her people's dwelling and to the east of the mosque. For this reason the Christians took the east as their qibla in their prayers, and they have no proof for that except innovation. Otherwise, the qibla of every worshipper of Allah is the Ka'bah, the Sacred House of Allah. His words, the Exalted: ﴿So she took a screen apart from them﴾, i.e., apart from her family, ﴿a screen﴾ to shield her from their eyes. When she did that, Allah the Exalted sent Jibril to her in the form of a man of perfect and well-proportioned creation. He entered upon her, and she said what Allah the Exalted related in His Book: ﴿Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing﴾, i.e., I seek protection in the Most Merciful, who has mercy on weak women like me, if you are a believer and God-fearing, then go away from me and do not frighten me or touch me with harm. Then Jibril, peace be upon him, said to her what Allah the Exalted reported, namely: ﴿He said: I am only the messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy﴾, i.e., pure, who has never been stained by any sin. She replied with what Allah the Exalted reported about her in His words: ﴿How can I have a boy﴾, i.e., by what means would a child come to me, ﴿when no man has touched me﴾, i.e., while I have not married, ﴿nor have I been unchaste﴾, i.e., nor have I been a fornicator. Jibril answered her with what Allah the Exalted reported in His words: ﴿He said: Thus it is﴾, i.e., the matter is as you have said, but your Lord said: ﴿It is easy for Me﴾, i.e., His creating him without a father, whether through marriage or through fornication, because it is easy for Us in one respect, ﴿and that We may make him a sign for mankind﴾, indicating Our power to create Adam without a father or a mother, and the resurrection in another respect. His words, the Exalted: ﴿and a mercy from Us; and it is a matter decreed﴾, i.e., that We make the promised boy a mercy from Us for everyone who believes in him and follows his way of faith and uprightness. This creation of the boy, which I have given to you, is a matter decreed, i.e., Allah has judged it and decreed it, so it is certain to come to be. Then Jibril blew into the opening of her garment, the breath reached her body, and she conceived him, as will be explained in the following verses.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Clarification of Maryam's nobility and her honor before her Lord.

2- The virtue of chastity and modesty.

3- That angels take forms as Allah the Exalted permits them.

4- The legitimacy of seeking refuge in Allah from everything feared, whether from a human or a jinn.

5- Piety prevents causing harm to people or inflicting injury upon them.

6- The creation of 'Isa is a clear sign in which the power of Allah the Exalted to create, both at the beginning and in return, is manifest.

**Explanation of the words:**

*So she withdrew with him:* that is, she secluded herself with him.

*To a remote place:* that is, far away from her people.

*And the pangs of childbirth drove her:* that is, the labour pains forced her and the pain of delivery compelled her.

*To the trunk of the palm tree:* so that she could lean on it while suffering the pains of labour.

*Forgotten and unremembered:* that is, a thing abandoned, neither known nor remembered.

*Then he called to her from beneath her:* that is, Jesus, peace be upon him, after she had given birth to him.

*Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream:* that is, a river called Sari.

*Fresh ripe dates:* fresh ripe dates (ruṭab janiyy) are those that are good and ready for picking.

*So eat and drink:* that is, eat of the dates and drink from the stream.

*And be consoled:* that is, be at peace of heart and rejoice in your child's birth, and do not grieve.

*I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast:* that is, abstaining from speech and silence.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues with the story of Maryam. After Jibril had given her the good news of a son, saying to her, "It is a matter already decreed," and breathed into the opening of her garment or the collar of her dress, she conceived immediately. ﴿So she withdrew with him to a remote place﴾, that is, she secluded herself with him in a distant place. ﴿Then the pangs of childbirth drove her﴾, that is, the pain of childbirth compelled her ﴿to the trunk of the palm tree﴾ so that she could lean on it while suffering the labour pains and their agonies. When she had given birth, she said, in regret and sorrow, what Allah, the Exalted, reported: ﴿Oh, I wish I had died before this and had been a thing forgotten﴾, that is, before this time when she had become a mother, and had been a thing abandoned, neither remembered nor known. At this point, ﴿he called to her from beneath her﴾, Jesus, peace be upon him, ﴿Do not grieve﴾, which encourages her to patience and consolation. And the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream﴾, that is, a river of water called Sari. ﴿And shake toward yourself the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you fresh ripe dates. So eat and drink﴾, that is, eat of the dates and drink from the river's water. ﴿And be consoled﴾, that is, be at peace of heart and rejoice in your son. ﴿And if you see any human being, say: Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast﴾, that is, silence. ﴿So I will not speak today to any human being﴾. All of this is from the words of Jesus to her, which Allah caused him to speak as an honour to her, to remove from her grief and psychological pain resulting from the birth, while she was a virgin who had not married.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Among the manifestations of Allah's power is her conception and delivery within the span of an hour of a day.

2. Affirmation of Allah's miracles (karamat) for His friends: Allah, the Exalted, honoured Maryam by making Jesus speak at the time of his birth, so he guided and gave her good news, removed pain and grief from her, caused a palm tree to bear fruit for her, and caused the river to flow for her after it had dried up.

3. Confirmation of the system of causes: what is within a person's capacity to do is to be done. Allah, the Exalted, caused the palm tree to bear fruit for Maryam, which was beyond her ability, then commanded her to shake the trunk of the palm tree so that fresh ripe dates would fall upon her, since this was within her power.

4. The legitimacy of vows (nadhr), but the vow of abstaining from speech has been abrogated (naskh, meaning the cancellation of a ruling by a later revelation) in Islam.

**Explanation of the words:**

*Fa-atat bihi* (she brought him): that is, she brought her child, ʿĪsā (Jesus), peace be upon him and upon her.

*Jiʾta shay'an fariyyā* (you have come with a monstrous thing): that is, a great matter, in that you have brought a child without a father.

*Yā ukhta Hārūn* (O sister of Hārūn): that is, O sister of the righteous man Hārūn (Aaron).

*Imra'a sawʾ* (a man of evil): that is, a man who commits immoral acts.

*Fa-ashārat ilayhi* (so she pointed to him): that is, to ʿĪsā, while he was in the cradle.

*Ātānī al-kitāb* (He has given me the Book): that is, the Injīl (Gospel), spoken of in terms of what will be in the future.

*Mubārakan aynamā kuntu* (blessed wherever I am): that is, wherever I am found there is blessing in me and with me, and people benefit through me.

*Wa-barran bi-wālidatī* (and dutiful to my mother): that is, kind to her and obedient to her, so that she receives no least harm from me.

*Jabbāran shaqiyyā* (domineering and wretched): that is, oppressive and arrogant, nor disobedient to my Lord, going outside of His obedience.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues with the story of Maryam (Mary) and her people. After she recovered, she carried her son and brought him to her people. As soon as they saw them, one of them said: ﴿O Maryam, you have certainly come with something monstrous﴾, meaning a grave matter, namely your bringing a child without a father. ﴿O sister of Hārūn﴾: they attributed her to a righteous servant of God called Hārūn. ﴿Your father was not a man of evil﴾, meaning Imrān, ﴿nor was your mother an unchaste woman﴾, meaning Ḥannah. That is, they said, how has this happened to you, when you are a daughter of a pure house and a noble family?

Then she pointed to ʿĪsā, the infant in his swaddling clothes. That is, she told them: ask him, and he will tell you the news and inform you of the truth, because she knew that he would speak, since he had earlier called out to her at the moment of his birth from beneath her, and said to her what the Exalted mentioned in the preceding verses.

They answered her, belittling her, rejecting her and marvelling at her: ﴿How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?﴾ Then God made the infant ʿĪsā speak, and he answered them with what God related of him in His words: ﴿He said: "Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet. He has made me blessed wherever I am, and has enjoined upon me prayer (ṣalāh) and zakāh (obligatory almsgiving) as long as I live. And He has made me dutiful to my mother, and has not made me domineering or wretched."﴾

He answered them with everything God had written and caused him to speak. ʿĪsā, as he related of himself, did not fall short in any of it. He was a servant of God, to whom the Injīl was revealed, and he was given prophethood and sent to the Children of Israel. He was blessed, healing the sick and raising the dead by God's permission. Blessing is gained through keeping his company, serving him, and believing in him and loving him. He maintained prayer and paid zakāh throughout his life. He was neither an oppressor nor a haughty tyrant, nor a rebellious disobeyer. Thus, as he himself reported, ﴿peace﴾ upon him, meaning complete security, on the day he was born, so that no devil touched him; on the day he dies, so that his grave is not tested; and on the day he is raised alive, so that the great terror does not grieve him. He will be among the secure and the blessed in the Abode of Peace.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1- Affirmation of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), and of the servanthood and prophethood of ʿĪsā, peace be upon them both.

2- A sign in the speech of ʿĪsā in the cradle and his report of the perfections God bestowed upon him.

3- The obligation to be dutiful to one's parents: treating them with kindness, obeying them in what is right, and withholding harm from them.

4- A condemnation of arrogance, pride, oppression, and wretchedness, which is rebellion and disobedience.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 19, verses 34–40:

Explanation of the words:

*Dhalika ʿIsa ibn Maryam* (That is ʿIsa, son of Maryam): that is, this one whose description I have made clear to you and whose account I have told you, is ʿIsa son of Maryam.

*Qawl al-haqq* (a word of truth): that is, and it is the word of truth which Allah, exalted is He, has informed of.

*Yamtarun* (they doubt): they are in doubt.

*Ma kana li-llahi an yattakhidha min walad* (It is not for Allah to take a son): that is, it is not befitting for Allah to take a son, and He is the One who says to a thing "Be," and it is.

*Subhanahu* (Glory be to Him): that is, exalted above having a son, a partner, a likeness or a equal.

*Sirat mustaqim* (a straight path): that is, a straight way whose traveler does not go astray.

*Fa-ikhtalafa al-ahzab* (Then the factions differed): that is, concerning ʿIsa. The Jews said he was a sorcerer and the son of adultery, and the Christians said he is God and the son of God, exalted is Allah above what they describe.

*Min mashhadi yawmin ʿazim* (from the scene of a tremendous day): this is the Day of Resurrection.

*Asmiʿ bihim wa-absir* (How much they will hear and see!): that is, how much I will make them hear and see on the Day of Resurrection when they witness the punishment.

*Wa-andhirhum yawm al-hasra* (And warn them of the Day of Regret): that is, warn them of what will occur on the Day of Resurrection of regret and remorse, when they see the people of Paradise inheriting their dwellings in it, while they inherit the dwellings of the people of Paradise in the Fire, so the regret will be great and the remorse will intensify.

Meaning of the verses:

After Allah, exalted is He, related the story of Maryam from the moment she withdrew from her family to a secluded place, devoted to her Lord, until she pointed to ʿIsa while he was in the cradle, and he spoke, saying: "Indeed I am the servant of Allah," Allah made clear that Jibril gave her good news, and that he breathed into the opening of her garment, so she conceived ʿIsa, and that he was born after an hour of her pregnancy, and that she gave birth to him beneath the trunk of a palm tree, and that he called to her from beneath her: "Do not grieve," and guided her to the statement she should make to her people when they asked her about her child born without a father, which was to point to him, asking them to question him. They did question him, and he answered that he is the servant of Allah, that He gave him the Scripture, made him a prophet, blessed him, and enjoined upon him prayer and zakat as long as he lives, and that he is dutiful to his mother, and was not an arrogant wretch. Allah, exalted is He, referred to this in His saying in this verse [34]: ﴿That is ʿIsa, son of Maryam﴾, that is, this one whose description I have made clear to you and whose account I have told you, is ʿIsa son of Maryam, and what I have informed you of is ﴿a word of truth about which they dispute﴾, that is, they are in doubt, for the Jews said about ʿIsa that he was the son of adultery and that he was a sorcerer, and the Christians said he is God and the son of God and the third of three, according to their various sects and factions. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not for Allah to take a son; glory be to Him﴾ negates from Him, exalted is He, the taking of a son. How could that be proper or fitting for Him, who is free of need for anything other than Himself, while everything else is needy of Him, and who says to a thing "Be," and it is? So ʿIsa, peace be upon him, came into being by Allah's word to him "Be," and it was. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ Allah, exalted is He, has declared Himself free of a son, a partner, a likeness, an equal, and of dependence and need on His creatures, by His saying: "Glory be to Him," that is, exalting Him above the attributes of created beings. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path﴾ [36].

This is from the speech of ʿIsa, peace be upon him, to the Children of Israel. He informed them that he is the servant of Allah, not the son of Allah, nor a god alongside Allah, and informed them that Allah, exalted is He, is his Lord and their Lord, so let them all worship Him with what He has legislated for them, and not worship anything with Him, for there is no god for them except Him, glory be to Him and exalted is He. He made known to them that this true belief and worship in accordance with what Allah has legislated is the path that leads its traveler to happiness, and whoever turns away from it and takes the path of shirk and error will be led to loss. And His saying in verse [37]: ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾, that is, concerning ʿIsa: some said he is God, some said he is the son of God, and some said he and his mother are two gods besides Allah. Those who uttered these statements disbelieved by them, so Allah, exalted is He, threatened them with a painful punishment, saying: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve﴾ by their attributing a son and a partner to Allah. "Woe" is a valley in Hell, so they will certainly enter it. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 19, verses 41–45:

Explanation of the words:

"And mention in the Book": i.e., in the Qur'an.

"Indeed he was a man of truth (siddiq)": i.e., one who was greatly truthful, having reached the highest degree of truthfulness.

"O my father": i.e., my father, who was Azar.

"A straight path": i.e., a straight way without any crookedness, leading you to Paradise.

"Do not worship Satan": i.e., do not obey him in his call to you to worship idols.

"Disobedient (asiyy)": i.e., one who disobeys Allah, Exalted, and transgresses His command.

"Then you would be a companion (waliyy) of Satan": i.e., close to him, a comrade to him in it, that is, the Fire.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the beginning of the story of Abraham the Friend (Khalil) of Allah, peace be upon him, with his father Azar, may the curses of the Most Merciful be upon him. Allah, the Exalted, said to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): "And mention," O our Prophet, "in the Book," i.e., the Noble Qur'an, "Abraham," Our friend, "indeed he was a man of truth," i.e., truthful in his sayings and deeds, having reached a great level of truthfulness, "a prophet" from Our prophets. So he is worthy of being mentioned in the Qur'an so that he may be a good example for the believers. And mention him "when he said to his father," Azar, "O my father, why do you worship" i.e., ask through supplication and draw near through various kinds of acts of devotion, "that which neither hears nor sees," the idols, i.e., it neither sees you nor hears you, "and it does not avail you anything," it does not repel harm from you nor bring you benefit, so what need do you have to worship it? "O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge" i.e., from my Lord, Exalted is He, "that which has not come to you," [so] "follow me" in what I believe, do and call to, "I will guide you to a straight path," i.e., a straight way that leads you to happiness and salvation. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 19, verses 46–50:

Explanation of the words:

*La'in lam tantahi* (If you do not desist): i.e., from confronting them and reviling them.

*La-arjumannaka* (I will surely stone you): with stones, or with foul speech, so beware of me.

*Wahjurni maliyyan* (And leave me for a long time): i.e., safe from my punishment.

*Salamun 'alayka* (Peace be upon you): i.e., a pledge of safety from me to you, that I will not return to you concerning what you dislike from me.

*Innahu kana bi hafiyya* (Indeed, He has always been gracious to me): i.e., kind to me, honouring me, answering me when I call upon Him.

*'Asa alla akuna bi du'a'i rabbi shaqiyya* (Perhaps I shall not be unblessed in my supplication to my Lord): rather, He will answer my supplication and grant my request.

*Falamma i'tazalahum* (So when he had withdrawn from them): by emigrating to the land of al-Quds and leaving them.

*Wahabna lahu Ishaq wa Ya'qub* (And We gave him Isaac and Jacob): i.e., We gave him two sons with whom he would find comfort, as a recompense from Us for his emigration from his people.

*Wawahabna lahum min rahmatina* (And We bestowed upon them of Our mercy): abundant good, wealth and offspring, along with prophethood and knowledge.

*Lisana sidqin 'aliyya* (A tongue of truth, exalted): i.e., elevated, in that they are praised and remembered with the finest qualities.

The meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the story of Ibrahim and his father Azar. After that gentle and noble call, with its good and courteous words, which Ibrahim addressed to his father Azar so that he would believe in and affirm the Oneness of God, and thereby be saved and find happiness, Azar answered him with expressions devoid of mercy and courtesy, filled instead with harshness, roughness, threat and menace. This is what God related of him in His saying, in verse [46]: ﴿He said: "Do you turn away from my gods, O Ibrahim?"﴾, i.e., do you dislike them and revile them? ﴿"If you do not desist"﴾, i.e., from confronting them with any evil, ﴿"I will surely stone you"﴾ with the most vile and abominable words, ﴿"And leave me for a long time"﴾, i.e., keep far from me as long as you are healthy, sound of body and whole, before there befalls you from me what you dislike. This was the reply of Azar, the disbelieving polytheist. As for Ibrahim, the believing monotheist, he answered with what God related of him in His saying in verse [47]: ﴿He said: "Peace be upon you"﴾, i.e., safety from me to you, O my father, so I will never return to you concerning what you dislike from me, and I will repay your evil with good. ﴿"I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord"﴾, i.e., I will ask Him to guide you to faith and monotheism, so that you repent and He forgives you. ﴿"Indeed, He has always been gracious to me"﴾, Glorified and Exalted is He, ﴿"kind to me, honouring me, who does not disappoint me in what I ask of Him."﴾

And His saying, related as the words of Ibrahim: ﴿"I will withdraw from you and from what you invoke besides God"﴾, i.e., I will go far away from you, leaving you and what you worship besides God of idols and images, ﴿"and I will call upon my Lord; perhaps I shall not be unblessed in my supplication to my Lord."﴾, i.e., my hope in my Lord is great that I will not be made wretched by worshipping Him as you were made wretched by worshipping idols. God, Most High, said, telling of him: when he fulfilled what he had promised them of his emigration to their lands, to the land of al-Quds, leaving his father, his family and his home, We recompensed him with the best, for We gave him two sons with whom he found comfort in his loneliness, namely Isaac and Jacob, each of whom We made a prophet and messenger. And We bestowed upon all of them, who were three in number, the father Ibrahim and his two sons Isaac and Jacob, son of Isaac, peace be upon them, of Our mercy, great good: wealth, offspring and goodly provision. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So when he had withdrawn from them and from what they worshipped besides God, We gave him Isaac and Jacob﴾, and Jacob was the son of his son Isaac, ﴿and each We made a prophet, and We bestowed upon them of Our mercy﴾.

And His saying concerning them: ﴿And We granted them a tongue of truth, exalted﴾. This is another favour in return for the emigration in the way of God, for God, Most High, granted them a tongue of truth in the Hereafter, so that all adherents of the divine religions praise Ibrahim and his descendants with the finest and most excellent praise. This is the exalted, elevated tongue of truth which Ibrahim and his two sons were honoured with, as an honour and favour from God Most High, a reward for Ibrahim's truthfulness and patience, and consequently for his emigration from the idols and their worshippers.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The distinction between what comes from the mouth of the believing monotheist of good speech, sound words, gentleness of manner and speech, and what comes from the mouth of the disbelieving polytheist of evil speech, vile words, harshness of manner and roughness of speech.

2- The legitimacy of parting peacefully and taking leave, which is to say to a wicked person, "Peace be upon you," not meaning by it a greeting, but meaning to leave him and what he is in.

3- The legitimacy of emigration and the explanation of its virtue; this emigration of Ibrahim was the first emigration on earth.

4- Encouragement toward a good reputation, that a person should have good praise among people for the good he has done and the benefit he has brought.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 19, verses 51–53:

Explanation of the words:

"And mention in the Book": i.e., in the Qur'an, as an honour and a glorification.

"Musa (Moses)": i.e., the son of 'Imran, the Prophet of the Children of Israel, peace be upon him.

"Mukhlasan" (sincere/chosen): i.e., chosen and selected, according to the reading with a fatha on the lam, "mukhlasan"; and devoted to his Lord, singling Him out for worship, reaching the highest stations in that, according to the reading with a kasra on the lam.

"Janib al-Tur" (the side of the Mount): al-Tur is a mountain in Sinai, between Madyan and Egypt.

"Wa qarabnahu najiyyan" (and We brought him near, as a confidant): i.e., We brought him near in an honouring and dignifying nearness, conversing with Us, spoken to by Us from before.

"Akhahu Harun nabiyyan" (his brother Harun, as a prophet): when he asked his Lord to give his brother the mission, so He granted it, made him a prophet, and sent him with him to Pharaoh.

Meaning of the verses:

This is a summary of the story of Musa, peace be upon him. Almighty God said, addressing His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And mention﴾ in this golden chain of God's righteous servants, the people of monotheism and certainty, Musa son of 'Imran, for he is worthy of mention in the Qur'an. The reason for this is His saying: ﴿Indeed, he was sincere﴾, i.e., chosen and selected to convey from Us to Our servants what they were created for, which is remembering Us and thanking Us: remembering Us with their tongues and hearts, and thanking Us with their limbs, by worshipping Us alone to the exclusion of anyone else. Musa was like this. And His saying: ﴿and he was a messenger, a prophet﴾, i.e., and among Our bounties upon him and Our honouring him is that We made him a prophet and messenger; We informed him of it and sent him to Pharaoh and his chiefs. ﴿And We called him﴾ while he was on his way from Madyan to Egypt, at the right side of the Mount, where We informed him and sent him; and thus ﴿We brought him near as a confidant﴾, so he began to converse with Us: We made him hear Our speech and he heard His speech. And how great is this honour! And His saying: ﴿And We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet﴾: this is another favour from God upon Musa the Prophet, when he asked his Lord to send his brother Harun with him to Pharaoh. By a mercy from God He answered him, informed Harun of prophethood and sent him with him as a messenger. This was only by a special mercy, for prophethood is not sought, nor is it attained through diligence in worship or through supplication and striving, for it is a special divine gift.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The virtue of sincerity (ikhlas), which is directing worship to God outwardly and inwardly.

2- Affirmation of the attribute of speech and intimate conversation for God, Exalted.

3- Demonstration of God's honour and favour toward Musa, for He gave him what He gave to no one among the worlds, by answering his supplication and making his brother Harun a prophet and messenger.

4- Establishing that every messenger is a prophet, but not the reverse; i.e., not every prophet is a messenger.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 19, verse 54–58:

Explanation of the words:

"And mention in the Book Ismail": i.e., mention in the Qur'an, honouring and magnifying him, Ismail ibn Ibrahim al-Khalil (peace be upon them both).

"True to his promise" (sadiq al-wa'd): he never broke a promise at all.

"With prayer and zakat": i.e., with establishing the prayer (iqamat al-salat) and giving zakat (ita' al-zakat).

"Pleasing": i.e., God the Exalted was pleased with his words and deeds, because of his certainty (yaqin) and sincerity (ikhlas).

"Idris": he is the grandfather of Abu Nuh (Noah), peace be upon him.

"And We raised him to a lofty station": to the fourth heaven.

"Israel": i.e., Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, peace be upon them all.

"And of those whom We guided and chose": i.e., among those whom We guided to Our path and chose by Our prophethood.

"When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them": i.e., when they are read to them while they listen to them.

"Prostrating and weeping" (sujjadan wa bukiyya): plural of sajid and baki, i.e., prostrating while weeping.

Meaning of the verses:

The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: just as you have been told about Maryam and her son, Ibrahim and Musa, mention likewise Ismail, for he ﴿was true to his promise﴾; he never broke a promise at all, and he would wait for the promised one for nights, standing in his place awaiting him. ﴿And he was a messenger and a prophet﴾: God informed him in Makkah al-Mukarramah, for he lived there, and He sent him to the Arab tribe of Jurhum, and from them he married and had children, and from his descendants was Muhammad ﷺ. As for the Exalted's words: ﴿And he used to enjoin his family to prayer and zakat﴾: by "family" is meant his household and his people of the tribe of Jurhum; by "prayer" is meant establishing it, and by "zakat" is meant paying it. This is among the things that elevated his status and raised his rank, so he deserved to be mentioned in the Mighty Qur'an. As for His words: ﴿And he was with his Lord pleasing﴾: this is another reason for honouring him and bestowing favour upon him by mentioning him in the Noble Qur'an in the line of the prophets and messengers. The meaning of ﴿And he was with his Lord pleasing﴾ is that all his sayings and deeds were accepted and pleasing, and thus he was pleasing to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. As for the Exalted's words: ﴿And mention in the Book Idris﴾, he is the grandfather of Abu Nuh, and he merited mention in the Qur'an because he ﴿was a man of truth﴾, abundantly truthful, to the extent that a lie never passed his tongue at all; and he was truthful in his actions and in what he did, so he knew nothing but truth in word or deed, and he was a prophet among the prophets of God. As for His words ﴿And We raised him to a lofty station﴾: to the fourth heaven during his lifetime, just as God raised Isa, and raised Muhammad to beyond the seventh heaven. As for the Exalted's words: ﴿Those are the ones upon whom God bestowed favour from among the prophets, of the descendants of Adam﴾, like Idris; ﴿and of those whom We carried with Nuh﴾, i.e., in the ark, like Ibrahim; ﴿and of the descendants of Ibrahim﴾, like Ishaq and Ismail; ﴿and Israel﴾, i.e., and of the descendants of Israel, like Musa, Harun, Dawud, Sulayman, Zakariyya, Yahya and Isa; ﴿and of those whom We guided﴾ to Our knowledge and Our path that leads to Our pleasure, through worship and sincerity to Us in it; ﴿and whom We chose﴾ for Our revelation and the bearing of Our message. As for His words ﴿When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fell down prostrating and weeping﴾: i.e., those whom We guided and chose, from among those whom We chose. Ijtiba' (choosing) means selection and elevation by taking the elite. ﴿When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them﴾, which carry admonitions, lessons, proofs and arguments, ﴿they fell down prostrating﴾ to God their Lord, ﴿and weeping﴾ over what they see of shortcoming or neglect in regard to their Lord, may His majesty be exalted and great.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The affirmation of prophethood, for the One who gave these prophets their message and sent them cannot be denied the right to send Muhammad as a prophet and messenger.

2- The virtue of commanding prayer and zakat.

3- The virtue of fulfilling promises and truthfulness in word and deed.

4- The sunnah of prostration for one who recites this verse or to whom it is recited while he listens to it. ﴿They fell down prostrating and weeping﴾

5- The virtue of weeping during prostration, for when 'Umar recited this verse he would prostrate and then say: "This is the prostration, so where is the weeping?", meaning the weeping.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 19, verses 59–63:

Explanation of the words:

Khalf (خلف): i.e., a bad successor (ʿaqib saw').

Adaʿu al-salah (أضاعوا الصلاة): they neglected it, leaving it aside, and by doing so they became disbelievers.

Ittaba'u al-shahawat (اتبعوا الشهوات): they plunged into sins and transgressions such as fornication and drinking wine.

Yalqawna ghayyan (يلقون غياً): i.e., a valley in Hell into which they will be cast.

Wa la yuzlamuna shay'an (ولا يظلمون شيئاً): i.e., they will not be deprived of any part of the reward for their good deeds.

Jannat ʿadn (جنات عدن): i.e., a lasting dwelling.

Bil-ghayb (بالغيب): i.e., He promised them these things while they are unseen by their eyes, because they are absent from them: they are in the heavens and they are on the earth.

Ma'tiyyan (مأتياً): i.e., His promise, which He makes to His servants, coming without doubt.

Laghwan (لغواً): i.e., superfluous speech, which is that which has no benefit in it.

Bukratan wa ʿashiyyan (بكرةً وعشياً): i.e., by their measure in the world; otherwise, Paradise has no sun, so there is no day and night in it.

Man kana taqiyyan (من كان تقياً): i.e., whoever was god-fearing in the life of this world, who did not abandon the obligatory duties and did not approach the forbidden things.

Explanation of the verses:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Then there succeeded them a bad successor⦈ inform us about those righteous people whom He chose and guided from among the prophets and their descendants: after them there came a bad successor, whose characteristic was that they ﴿neglected the prayer﴾; some of them delayed it beyond its times, and some of them abandoned it altogether; ﴿and followed their appetites﴾, so they plunged into the mire of vices: they drank intoxicants, bore false witness, consumed what is forbidden, indulged in amusements and games, committed fornication and immorality, after the passing of those righteous people, as is the state of the Christians and Jews today, and even many Muslims. Concerning these bad successors, the Most High informs that ﴿they will soon meet Ghayy﴾ after entering the fire of Hell. As for al-Ghayy: it has been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that it is a well in Hell, and from Ibn Mas'ud that it is a valley in Hell; both are sound, for a well may be found in a valley, and wells are often found in valleys.

The words of the Most High: ﴿Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds; those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged in the least﴾: that is, but whoever repents from this bad successor, believes, i.e., realizes his faith, and does righteous deeds, performing the obligatory duties and abstaining from the forbidden things. ﴿Those⦈, i.e., these penitent and turning-back ones, ﴿will enter Paradise⦈ together with their righteous predecessors, ﴿and will not be wronged in the least⦈, i.e., they will not be deprived of, nor diminished in, any part of the reward of their deeds.

The words of the Most High: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence⦈, i.e., gardens of everlasting abode, ﴿which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen⦈, i.e., He promised them these, while they are unseen by them, as they have not seen them, because they are in the heavens and they are on the earth.

His words: ﴿Indeed, His promise is ever fulfilled⦈: i.e., their not having seen it does no harm, because what the Most Merciful has promised never fails; it must be attained, and the meaning of ma'tiyyan is that its owner will certainly reach it.

The words of the Most High in verse [62]: ﴿They will not hear therein any idle talk⦈ inform us that those penitent ones who believed, did righteous deeds, and entered Paradise will not hear therein, i.e., in Paradise, any laghw, which is false speech and any speech with no good in it, except for the greeting; they will receive it from the angels and hear it from them, and this is among the spiritual bliss of Paradise, the abode of bliss.

The words of the Most High: ﴿And they will have their provision therein morning and evening⦈, i.e., they will have their food therein, which is whatever their souls desire of delicious food and drink, ﴿morning and evening⦈, i.e., at the time of the morning meal and the time of the evening meal in the world; for in Paradise there is no night and no day, but only lights. It is permissible that when the time of the morning or evening meal arrives, the lights change from one color to another, or the doors are closed and the curtains lowered, and this serves as a sign of the time of the meal and the evening meal.

The words of the Most High in verse [63]: ﴿That is the Paradise⦈ — He points to the Paradise, the abode of peace — ﴿which We cause to inherit from Our servants whoever was god-fearing⦈ among them. As for the wicked, their station therein is inherited by the god-fearing, just as the station of the god-fearing in the Fire is inherited by a wicked one among the wicked; for this is the meaning of inheritance: this one inherits that, and that one inherits this. Indeed, every person has a station in Paradise and a place in the Fire; whoever believes and does righteous deeds enters Paradise and occupies his station; whoever disbelieves, associates partners with God, and does evil enters the Fire and occupies his place therein. God the Most High makes the god-fearing inherit the stations of the wicked which were theirs in Paradise.

Lessons from the verses:

1- Condemnation of the bad successor, who neglects the prayer and follows the appetites.

2- Severe warning for those who plunge into appetites and abandon the prayer, and die in that state.

3- The door of repentance is open, and repentance is accepted from everyone who seeks it and repents.

4- Explanation of the bliss of Paradise, the abode of the god-fearing and the righteous.

5- Affirmation of the principle of inheritance between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire.

6- Clarification that the heirs of Paradise are the god-fearing, and the heirs of the Fire are the wicked.

Explanation of the words:

*And we do not descend* (wa-ma natanazzalu): al-tanazzul is descent, occurring time after time.

*Except by the command of your Lord* (illa bi-amri rabbika): that is, except by His permission to us to descend upon whomever He wills.

*To Him belongs what is before us* (lahu ma bayna aydina): that is, of the matters of the Hereafter that are yet to come.

*And what is behind us* (wa-ma khalfana): that is, what has passed of the world.

*And what is between that* (wa-ma bayna dhalika): of what has not yet passed of the world until the Day of Resurrection; that is, He has knowledge of all of it.

*And your Lord was not forgetful* (wa-ma kana rabbuka nasiyya): that is, one who forgets. He, exalted is He, does not forget, so how would He forget you and abandon you?

*Lord of the heavens and the earth* (rabbu al-samawati wal-ard): that is, their Owner and the One who disposes of them.

*And be steadfast in His worship* (wa-isṭabir li-ibadatihi): that is, be patient and endure patience in His worship until death.

*Do you know of any namesake for Him?* (hal ta'lamu lahu samiyyan): that is, He has no namesake, no like, and no equal; He is Allah, the One, "He has not been begotten, nor has He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him."

Meaning of the two verses:

The occasion of revelation of these two verses is what is related and widely transmitted: revelation was delayed from the Prophet ﷺ, and the one who brings revelation is Jibril (peace be upon him). When he came after a delay, the Prophet ﷺ said to him, "What prevents you from visiting us more often than you visit us?" Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed His words in answer to the Prophet's ﷺ question: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord﴾, O Messenger, that is, except by His permission to us. None of us may descend from one heaven to another, or to the earth, except by the permission of our Lord, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿To Him belongs what is before us, and what is behind us, and what is between that﴾, that is, He has the command and knowledge of what is before us, namely the matters of the Hereafter, and what is behind us, namely what has passed of the world, in knowledge and in management; and what is between that, until the Day of Resurrection, in knowledge and management. ﴿And your Lord was not forgetful﴾, O Messenger of Allah, forgetting you or abandoning you, for forgetfulness is not an attribute of His, so that He would forget.

As for His words, exalted is He: ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them﴾, He informs His Messenger that He is the Owner of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and the One who disposes of them; everything belongs to Him, is in His hand, under His control, and subject to His rule. ﴿So worship Him﴾, O Messenger, in the manner He has commanded you to worship Him. ﴿And be steadfast in His worship﴾, that is, bear its hardships, for there is no god but Him. Then ﴿Do you know of any namesake for Him?﴾, that is, any equal or like? The answer is no. Therefore worship Him alone and bear in His path whatever you are able to bear, for there is no one worthy of worship except Him, since all else besides Him is a creature under His lordship, subject to His judgment and management.

Guidance from the two verses:

1. Affirmation of Allah's dominion over all creation, His knowledge of all creation, and His power over all of that.

2. The impossibility of forgetfulness for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

3. Affirmation of Allah's lordship over all the worlds, and by this His divinity is made obligatory upon all the worlds.

4. The obligation to worship Allah, and the obligation to be steadfast in it until death.

5. The negation of any likeness, equal, or peer for Allah, for He is Allah, the One, to whom no one is equal.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 19, verses 66–72:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And man says﴾: i.e., the disbeliever in the meeting with Allah, the Exalted.

﴿And he was nothing﴾: i.e., before He created him, he had no essence, no name, and no attribute.

﴿Jathiyyan (kneeling)﴾: i.e., crouching upon their knees in humiliation, fear and grief.

﴿From every shi'ah (party)﴾: i.e., every group that cooperated in falsehood and supported one another in it.

﴿'Itiyyan (rebelliously)﴾: i.e., arrogance against worshipping Him and oppression of His servants.

﴿Awla bihā ṣiliyyan (most deserving of it to burn)﴾: i.e., most deserving of being roasted, burned and punished in the Fire.

﴿Illā wāriduhā (except that you will pass over it)﴾: i.e., passing by it. If one falls into it, he perishes; if he passes by and does not fall, he is saved.

﴿Ḥatman maqḍiyyan (a decree decided)﴾: i.e., a matter that Allah has decreed, judged and made binding, so it is certain to occur.

﴿Fīhā jithiyyan (kneeling therein)﴾: i.e., in the Fire, crouching upon their knees, some close to others.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 19, verses 66–72:

﴿Jathiyyan (kneeling)﴾: i.e., crouching upon their knees in humiliation, fear and grief.

﴿From every shi'ah (party)﴾: i.e., every group that cooperated in falsehood and supported one another in it.

﴿'Itiyyan (rebelliously)﴾: i.e., arrogance against worshipping Him and oppression of His servants.

﴿Awla bihā ṣiliyyan (most deserving of it to burn)﴾: i.e., most deserving of being roasted, burned and punished in the Fire.

﴿Illā wāriduhā (except that you will pass over it)﴾: i.e., passing by it. If one falls into it, he perishes; if he passes by and does not fall, he is saved.

﴿Ḥatman maqḍiyyan (a decree decided)﴾: i.e., a matter that Allah has decreed, judged and made binding, so it is certain to occur.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 19, verses 73–76:

Explanation of the words:

"Our clear verses": that is, the clear verses of the Qur'an, its manifest proofs and evidences.

"Better in station": whether we or you; "maqam" means a dwelling-place, a place of residence, and here it is meant as rank.

"And better in assembly (nadiyy)": that is, a gathering place (nadi), the meeting place of the noble and the place of consultation and exchange of opinions.

"Better in furnishings and appearance (ri'yan)": that is, in wealth, goods and outward show.

"Either the punishment or the Hour": that is, by killing and captivity; and as for "the Hour," it is the Resurrection, which includes the Fire of Hell.

"Who is worse in place": that is, in rank.

"And weaker in forces (jund)": that is, fewer helpers.

"And better in outcome (marad)": that is, what one returns to and comes back to, which is the bliss of Paradise.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to establish prophethood, monotheism and the Final Resurrection. Almighty God says: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them﴾, that is, when they are recited to the disbelievers of Quraysh who deny monotheism, the prophethood of Muhammad, the Resurrection and the requital on the Day of Judgment, when the Messenger of God or one of the believers among his companions recites to them some of the clear verses of the Qur'an, clear in their meanings and proofs for monotheism, prophethood and the Resurrection, ﴿those who disbelieved say to those who believed: "Which of the two groups is better in station and finer in assembly?"﴾. This their saying is merely a reaction, for when they hear verses that carry the promise for the believers and the threat for disbelievers like them, they find nothing with which to ease the pain of their souls, so they say this. ﴿Which of the two groups﴾, that is, the group of the believers or the group of the disbelievers, is ﴿better in station﴾, that is, in dwelling and residence, and ﴿finer in assembly﴾, that is, in gathering place where people meet? For they compare the dwellings of the poor believers with the house of al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam, where the Messenger ﷺ and the believers gathered, and they compare them with the houses and dwellings of Abu Sufyan and the wealthy of Mecca and the assembly of Quraysh, which was their council. So God replied to them with His saying: ﴿How many generations before them did We destroy, who were better in furnishings and appearance!﴾, that is, let not this deceive them, the boasting and arrogance in which they indulge, for it will not last for them as long as they wage war against the call to truth and those who uphold it. How many peoples of past generations did We destroy when they did wrong, though they were better than these in wealth, goods and fine, beautiful appearance.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension﴾, that is, remind them, O Our Messenger, of Our custom with Our servants: whoever is in the error of polytheism, wrongdoing, arrogance and obstinacy, the custom of the Most Merciful regarding him is that He extends for him, meaning He gives him respite and lets him go on, as a gradual leading on, until, when they reach the appointed time in which they will be seized with punishment as the recompense of their disbelief, wrongdoing and obstinacy, it is either a worldly punishment by killing, captivity or the like, or the punishment of the Hereafter by the coming of the Hour, when they will be gathered to Hell blind, dumb and deaf, as recompense for their haughtiness and boasting. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿until, when they see what they are promised, either the punishment or the Hour, then they will know who is worse in place and weaker in forces﴾, that is, who is worse in rank and fewer in helpers: are they the disbelievers or the believers? But by then knowledge will not benefit, for remedy is no longer possible, and there is nothing left but regret and remorse.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah increases those who are guided in guidance﴾, that is, if the recitation of the clear verses moves the polytheists to obstinacy and arrogance because of the darkness of their disbelief, so they increase in disbelief and obstinacy, then the guided believers increase in guidance through them, because they carry guidance for them in every sentence and word, and they, through the radiance of their souls with faith, see the proofs, arguments and demonstrations which the verses contain, so their faith increases and their guidance grows in walking the path of happiness and perfection by performing the obligations and avoiding what is forbidden.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the lasting good deeds are better with your Lord﴾, O Messenger, ﴿in reward and better in return﴾. In this verse is consolation for the Messenger and the believers: that what the polytheists boast of in wealth, goods and fine circumstances is worth nothing before faith and righteous deeds, for wealth is perishing while the righteous deeds endure. So the reward of the lasting righteous deeds, which are acts of worship and obedience, is better than all the goods of this world, and ﴿better in return﴾, that is, better as something returned to its doer, for it is Paradise, the abode of peace, honor and blessing.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Uncovering the psychology of the disbelievers, which is pride in wealth and power, when the believers take pride in faith and its fruits in this world and the Hereafter, including a good outcome.

2- Explaining God's custom of granting respite to wrongdoers and letting them go on, as a gradual leading on for them, until they perish as losers.

3- Explaining God's custom of increasing the faith of the believers upon hearing the Noble Qur'an, or upon witnessing God's seizing of the wrongdoers.

4- Explaining the excellence of the lasting righteous deeds, among them: Subhan Allah (Glory be to God), al-Hamdu lillah (Praise be to God), la ilaha illa Allah (there is no god but God), Allahu akbar (God is greatest), and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah (there is no power nor strength except with God).

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 19, verses 88–95:

Explanation of the words:

"And they say, 'The Most Merciful has taken a son'": that is, the Arabs said the angels are the daughters of God, and the Christians said Jesus is the son of God.

"You have certainly produced a thing grotesque (idda)": that is, something abominable and monstrous.

"The heavens are about to burst apart (yatafattarna) from it": that is, they would split because of the enormity of this saying and the severity of its ugliness.

"And the mountains collapse (takharru al-jibalu hadda)": that is, they would fall down and be demolished and crushed.

"That they attribute to the Most Merciful a son": that is, because of their claim that the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic, has a son.

"And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful": that is, it is not proper for Him, nor does it befit Him, to have that, because He is the Lord and Sovereign of everything.

"There is not one in the heavens and earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant (abdan)": that is, submissive and compliant, whoever he may be.

"Alone (fardan)": that is, with nothing with him, neither wealth, nor authority, nor helper.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to address the statements of the people of polytheism and ignorance and the refutation of them by the Truth, blessed and exalted. Allah, the Most High, says, reporting about them: "And they say" (waqalu), that is, those disbelievers, "The Most Merciful has taken a son" (ittakhadha al-Rahmanu waladan), when some Arab tribes said the angels are the daughters of Allah, the Jews said Uzayr is the son of Allah, and the Christians said the Messiah is the son of Allah. After mentioning their saying, Allah says to them: "You have certainly produced a thing grotesque (shay'an idda)," that is, you have brought forth something abominable and monstrous. "The heavens are about to burst apart from it (yatafattarna minhu)," that is, they would split from it because of the ugliness and evil of this saying. "And the earth would split and the mountains would collapse in ruin (hadda)," that is, fall down because of the enormity of this saying, for it angers the Almighty, Mighty and Majestic. Had it not been for His forbearance and mercy, the whole universe would have been touched by painful punishment. And His saying: "That they attribute to the Most Merciful a son," that is, that they ascribe to the Most Merciful a son. "And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful," that is, it is not proper for Him, nor does it befit His majesty and perfection, to have a son, because a child is the result of a violent animal desire that drives the male to approach the female, so that by the permission of Allah a child comes into being; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is far above resembling His creatures. How could He resemble them when He is their Creator and the One who brought them into existence from nothing?

And His saying, Exalted is He: "There is not one in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant (abdan)." This is a proof of the falsehood of the saying of the disbelieving ignorant ones, for the one whom everyone in the heavens and the earth, from angels, humans and jinn, comes to on the Day of Resurrection as a submissive, humbled, compliant servant, how could he be conceived of as having taken a son? For a son is sought because of need for him, while the One free of need from all His creation has no need of a servant of His servants to say, "This is my son." O Allah, we disown before You what the ignorant, who are astray from the path of Your guidance, say about You.

And His saying, Exalted is He: "Indeed He has enumerated them and counted them precisely (ahsahum wa 'addahum 'adda)," that is, He knows them one by one; so if there were with Him a god, or if He had a son, He would know it. This is another proof of the falsehood of that ignorant, false, corrupt claim. And His saying: "And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone (fardan)." This is a refutation of those who claim that if they are resurrected they will have wealth, children, intercessors and helpers. He, Exalted, informs that not one of them will fail to come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone, with no intercessor or helper with him, and no wealth or authority.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The gravity of lying against Allah by ascribing a son or a partner to Him, or speaking about Him without knowledge.

2- Clarification that all creatures, from the greatest to the least, have among them nothing but servants of Allah; so ascribing a human, a jinn or an angel to Allah, the Exalted, is ascribing a servant to a Lord who is Owner, Subduer, Mighty and Wise.

3- Clarification of Allah's encompassing knowledge of His creation and His knowledge of their number, so that none of them is hidden from His knowledge, and no one among them is absent from the station of the Resurrection, for all come to Allah, the Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection alone.

This is another proof of the falsehood of that ignorant, false, corrupt claim. And His saying: "And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone (fardan)." This is a refutation of those who claim that if they are resurrected they will have wealth, children, intercessors and helpers. He, Exalted, informs that not one of them will fail to come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone, with no intercessor or helper with him, and no wealth or authority.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The gravity of lying against Allah by ascribing a son or a partner to Him, or speaking about Him without knowledge.

2- Clarification that all creatures, from the greatest to the least, have among them nothing but servants of Allah; so ascribing a human, a jinn or an angel to Allah, the Exalted, is ascribing a servant to a Lord who is Owner, Subduer, Mighty and Wise.

3- Clarification of Allah's encompassing knowledge of His creation and His knowledge of their number, so that none of them is hidden from His knowledge, and no one among them is absent from the station of the Resurrection, for all come to Allah, the Exalted, on the Day of Resurrection alone.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 19, verses 96–98:

Explanation of the words:

Wudd (wadd): that is, love, so that they live in mutual affection among themselves, and their Lord, exalted is He, loves them.

﴿Fa-innama yassarnahu bi-lisanika﴾: that is, We made the Qur'an easy, meaning its recitation and understanding, in your Arabic language.

Qawman ludda (qawman lundda): that is, people who are fierce adversaries, strong in quarrelling and disputing with falsehood, and they are the disbelievers of Quraysh.

Wa kam ahlakna: that is, many of the people of the generations before them, We destroyed them.

Hal tuhissu minhum min ahad: that is, do you find any of them?

Aw tasma'u lahum rikza: that is, a faint sound; and the answer is "no," because the interrogation is one of denial.

Meaning of the verses:

He, exalted is He, informs that those who believe in Allah, His Messenger, and the promise and threat of Allah, and who turn away from polytheism and disbelief and do righteous deeds, which are performing the obligatory duties and many of the voluntary acts, for these, He, exalted is He, informs that He will place in the hearts of His believing servants love and affection for them, and He, glorified and exalted, has done so. So the people of faith and righteous deeds love and are kind to one another, and this mutual affection among them is the fruit of the love of Allah, exalted is He, for them. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿So indeed, We have made it easy﴾: that is, this Qur'an, which the polytheists denied, We have made its recitation easy for you, since We revealed it in your tongue, ﴿that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous﴾ among Our believing servants, those who guarded themselves against the punishment of Allah through faith and righteous deeds after abandoning polytheism and sins, ﴿and warn thereby a people most contentious﴾, and they are the disbelievers of Quraysh, who were fierce and strong in disputing and quarrelling. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And how many generations have We destroyed before them﴾: that is, and many of the people of the generations before your people, We destroyed them when they denied Our messengers and opposed Our call, ﴿Do you perceive any of them, or hear from them a faint sound?﴾: that is, do you see them with your eye, or touch them with your hand, or hear from them a faint sound? No. Would that your people remembered this and took heed, and repented to their Lord through faith in Him, His Messenger, and the meeting with Him, and abandoned polytheism and sins.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The greatest glad tiding carried by the first verse is the love of Allah and His friends for whoever believes and does righteous deeds.

2- Clarification that the Qur'an was made easy by being revealed in the language of the Prophet (ﷺ), for the sake of giving good tidings to the people of faith and righteous deeds and warning to the people of polytheism and sins.

3- Warning the obstinate and tyrannical among people that there will befall them what befell those before them of destruction and ruin, and reality is a witness: where are the people of the earlier generations?
